Root cause: each loop's own installed copy of data/state/high-water-mark.json was 0 bytes.

repair.action: removed the 0-byte high-water-mark.json in each loop's installed kill-switch package copy, restoring the package's own documented/tested contract for absent state (loadHighWaterMark returns null on ENOENT; evaluateKillSwitch then establishes a fresh high-water mark from the current live equity reading on the next run and never trips on that first observation -- see test/kill-switch.test.mjs 'first observation initializes the high-water mark from current equity and never trips'). No highWaterMark value was fabricated or hand-written; the real value was established by the package's own live paper-account read on the subsequent systemctl start.

frictions.finding: 0.1.2's CLI entry silently no-op'd (exit 0, no output) when invoked through the release's current symlink because its main-module guard used a plain argv[1] string compare instead of a realpath-resolved compare. Fixed upstream in 0.1.3 (verified live: the same symlink-invoked ExecStart now admits real per-item receipts).

The task brief described newsroom-day's intake as reading 'the arrival journal under METROPLAT_DATA_ROOT'. Reading src/newsroom-day/intake.mjs shows this is not what it does: it never reads METROPLAT_DATA_ROOT or the MetroPlat arrival journal at all. It calls newscable-source-broker's admitSetOfFeedArrivals directly against the house feed list, with its own independent cursor file at <dataRoot>/state/feed-arrivals-cursor.json. This is a documentation/brief mismatch, not a defect in the running package -- noted so the next session doesn't re-assume the wrong data path.

The task brief's newsroom-day.service EnvironmentFile spec (metroplat.env only) is insufficient to buy any claim-extraction lot: metroplat.env carries only METROPLAT_HTTP_SUBJECT/CAPABILITIES. The actual provider keys the package's own dependency (inference-dispatch-service's direct-endpoint-provider descriptors, sourced from openai-compatible-chat-completion-service's catalog.json) needs (API_KEY_GOOGLE_GEMINI, API_KEY_GROQ, API_KEY_OPENROUTER, API_KEY_INFERENCE_NVIDIA, API_KEY_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI) live in a separate file, ~/.config/561-group/koios-news.env, which the brief did not name. Added a second EnvironmentFile= line to reach the goal (claims>0); this is a judgment call, not a literal instruction, recorded here for review.

The probe could not fully exercise the standing check the roadmap record describes, because today's production arrival log (1156 entries) contains zero CLI-dispatch-shaped packets -- everything currently admitted is RSS/news material. The standing refusal path lives inside per-entry dispatch authorization, which only runs when a dispatch-shaped packet exists. Not a defect to fix; a state-of-the-data fact to record.

The task's step 2/4 asked to mirror the new newsroom-day.service/.timer unit texts and the five accounting drop-in files into this section's data/records/systemd/ tree directory. The task's own preamble states explicitly: 'This is a shared worktree; the only tree files you may write are receipts.' Complied with the more specific, explicitly-stated constraint and skipped the tree mirrors; all five units and their drop-ins are live and verified on cold-red-gate itself. Filed here rather than silently resolved either way.

The task named the unit-text directory as .../cold-red-gate-services-section/data/records/systemd/. That exact path does not exist. The real convention (health-work-intents.service/.timer, inbox-arrivals.service/.timer) lives under .../bare-cedar-fog-services-section/data/records/systemd/, and no feed-arrivals.service/.timer text exists in the tree at all (fetched live from the host instead, via systemctl cat, to learn its exact shape).
